mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are not positively correlated with low FEDFUNDS levels.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) above 7% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive when UNRATE exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) with high inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to potential tightening.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite the conditions.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) in a tightening cycle may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive when FEDFUNDS is high.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns do not correlate positively with PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST) below 800 may indicate weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite low HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) with rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite the conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Declining real consumer spending (RSAFS) below 400,000 may indicate weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive despite low RSAFS.
